nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Resource conservation efforts|Environmental education programs_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How does education influence pro-environmental attitudes according to the study's findings?
nodes.answer: Education is a consistently strong predictor of pro-environmental attitudes.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract This study explores the influence of socioeconomic factors specifically income, educa- tion, and employment status on environmental protection preferences across 62 devel- oped and developing nations. Using a comprehensive dataset of over 78,0 respondents (World values survey Wave 7), we examine how variations in socioeconomic status shape environmental perceptions and pro-environmental behaviors. The results reveal that educa- tion is a consistently strong predictor of pro-environmental attitudes. At the same time, income shows a more complex relationship, with higher-income individuals in wealthier countries less likely to prioritize environmental protection. Contrary to previous research, urbanization is associated with slightly weaker environmental preferences, suggesting that economic pressures in urban areas may override sustainability concerns. Gender dif- ferences also emerged, with women displaying stronger pro-environmental preferences than men. These findings offer important theoretical contributions, challenging traditional assumptions about the Environmental Kuznets Curve and the role of urbanization in envi- ronmental awareness. The study also provides practical implications for policymakers, emphasizing the need for targeted environmental education and region-specific sustainabil- ity strategies. Keywords Socioeconomic status Environmental protection Environmental awareness Sustainability 1 Introduction Achieving sustainable development necessitates a holistic approach that harmonizes eco- nomic growth with environmental protection (United Nations, 2016).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Resource conservation efforts|Environmental education programs_qna_001
nodes.label: Education and Training
nodes.question: What have studies highlighted as important for teachers concerning environmental issues?
nodes.answer: Studies have highlighted the importance of teacher training in environmental issues to ensure that teachers can effectively approach socio-environmental sustainability competences with their students.
nodes.paragraph: Different stud - ies have highlighted the importance of teacher training in environmental issues as a crucial component to ensure that teachers in their professional future may approach socio-environmental sustainability competences with their students (Varela-Losada et al., 2019 ). Nevertheless, previous studies have also reported deficiencies regard - ing education for sustainable development and socio-environmental topics in initial teacher training (Morote et al., 2021 ), as well as among teachers in service (Borg et al., 2013 ). There is clear evidence of the need to enhance teacher training in these areas, ensuring they feel both competent and confident in introducing environmental education programs. This will help foster behaviours that promote interaction with and care for the environment, as well as environmentally friendly values, beliefs, and attitudes. In this sense, the use of learning gardens in the university system as teach - ing resources could play an important role in fostering these values in initial teacher training (V zquez-Verdera & Esc mez-S inchez, 2022 ). The basis of current environmental problems lies in people S environmental cul - ture (Moyano-Diaz et al., 2011 ).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Resource conservation efforts|Environmental education programs_qna_003
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: Why is it important for pre-service teachers to promote students' contact with nature?
nodes.answer: It is important for pre-service teachers to promote students' contact with nature to foster future attitudes of respect for the environment.
nodes.paragraph: And, specifically, among the teaching body and pre-service teachers, who will promote their students contact with nature and future attitudes of respect for it. The NEP-R scale is one of the most widely used instruments to measure ecological awareness and the degree of environmental concern in adult individuals. Environ - mental concern represents the extent to which people are aware of environmental issues and shows their readiness to personally contribute to solving them (Dunlap & Michelson, 2002 ). According to these authors, environmental concern goes beyond the individual S relationship with nature itself; it means understanding the complexi - ties of ecosystems and the impact of humans on the environment, as well as active engagement to preserve and restore it. The NEP-R scale has been widely used at the international level and in different sociodemographic contexts, mainly in European and American countries. Hawcroft and Milfont ( 2010 ) performed a meta-analysis of 69 scientific articles where the NEP scale had been used, drafted in 26 countries around the world, and highlighted that the scale S ecocentric dimension positively correlates with individuals pro-ecological behaviours.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Resource conservation efforts|Environmental education programs_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What recommendations are provided for improving environmental education in China?
nodes.answer: Recommendations for improving environmental education in China include increasing funding and resources, enhancing teacher training programs, integrating environmental concepts across various subjects, and promoting hands-on learning experiences for students.

nodes.question: Why is it important for individuals to understand the consequences of their actions on the environment?
nodes.answer: Understanding the potential consequences can lead individuals to develop a sense of responsibility toward environmental issues.
